payload.pattern: arc-profile registry resolution silently waives the CANON-007 staging gate in BOTH directions
payload.solution: scripts/arc-profile.mjs resolves PROJECT_REGISTRY as path.join(import.meta.dirname,'..','portfolio','PROJECT_REGISTRY.json'). That single line is wrong from either side. (1) Running the studio-ops copy from a sibling (node ../vaultspark-studio-ops/scripts/arc-profile.mjs) resolves PROJECT STATE from studio-ops, so the control plane's profile is reported as if it were the caller's - observed returning stagingType:none for a repo that has staging, which waives the 'verify on staging FIRST' gate. (2) Copying it locally verbatim - which the arc skill's own section 1b explicitly recommends - makes the registry path point at <project>/portfolio/PROJECT_REGISTRY.json, a portfolio file only studio-ops owns. It is missing, the profile falls back to inference, and canon measured registryMatched:false type:infrastructure hasStaging:false. Same waived gate, opposite cause. FIX: resolve the registry from the CONTROL PLANE (this repo if it is studio-ops, else the ../vaultspark-studio-ops sibling) while keeping project state resolved from the target dir, and emit a registrySource field so an unreachable control plane is visible as 'unreachable' instead of masquerading as an inferred hasStaging:false. Canon S307 implemented exactly this in its local copy; the same patch belongs in the control-plane original and in the arc skill's section 1b guidance, which currently recommends the local copy without noting it loses registry matching.

payload.headline: A two-state measurement plane published a confident 0% about 36 repos nobody had read
lessons: A score is a ratio over what was MEASURED; null never 0 when nothing was, and record coverage so a partial run cannot report a clean fleet
Count the readers before fixing the producer: 5 coercions existed for one defect, twice in the reader alone
A measurement must not lose to the absence of one: where two lanes upsert the same dated artifact, the blind lane must never overwrite the sighted one
A model term whose input is absent for EVERY row is a dead dimension, invisible because the output still looks like a number
PROVEN-INERT and PROMISE-IMPOSSIBLE need different consequences: the second asks for the remedy to be re-scoped or BUILT, not re-run

payload.pattern: A justification nobody executes is not evidence — a deferral list is a falsifiable claim about the world and must be checked like one.
payload.solution: docs/TEST_SCOPE.json excluded 82 tests from the suite, each with a free-text reason no gate had ever run. Measured: 14 passed locally (deferral bought nothing), 2 named files that do not exist, and tier1-windows-hide.mjs — the arc §0 / CANON-016 ABSOLUTE window-storm guard — was deferred as a studio-ops control-plane contract while walking THIS repo tree, failing here since S82 with 4 direct child_process imports under a green board. Fix shipped: scripts/check-test-scope-honesty.mjs executes every declared deferral and classifies it by observed behaviour; a deferral must now declare requires[] naming an artifact that is genuinely absent, and an entry with no requires[] is reported as unfalsifiable debt rather than trusted. Wired as an advisory doctor probe. Every propagated repo carrying TEST_SCOPE.json very likely carries the same unmeasured prose.

payload.headline: 79 writes reported saves that never happened — including a billing path where a charged customer could silently stay on free
payload.impact: supabase-js RETURNS { error } instead of throwing, so try/catch around a write is a false safety net: the catch is unreachable for the real failure and the success path always runs. 79 call sites across web, mobile, API routes and the Stripe webhook discarded it. The Stripe grant-Pro-tier write also answered 200 on failure, so Stripe recorded delivery and never retried. Mechanized as a guard that deliberately does NOT exempt try/catch. Separately: a drift checker shipped two sessions ago was wired into NOTHING and sat unrun while the drift it existed to catch recurred behind a green board — a doctor row alone never increments blockingFailing. Any repo using supabase-js or authoring guards should check both.
